newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A suspected drug lord who recently gave himself up to the police and appeared before the legislature on Tuesday said the congressional public hearings were "mere lip service and a cover-up for the failure of Congress to support the military and police fight against drug trafficking." (MANILA STANDARD)
- House of Representatives Speaker Jose de Venecia announced his bid for the presidency on Tuesday in the presence of 10,000 supporters. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Police investigators said at a congressional hearing that a suspected drug lord said to have recently slipped out of the country made telephone calls to two senators. One of the senators said there is a campaign to link him to trafficking of illegal drugs in the country. (INQUIRER)

- The Supreme Court which has twice rejected petitions for a people's initiative to amend the Constitution, decided on Tuesday to hear a third petition as a "new and separate case." Opposition congressmen, however, scored a major victory when they succeeded in blocking the inclusion among priority measures of the resolution convening Congress as a constituent assembly to amend the Constitution. (TODAY/PHILIPPINE STAR/MANILA TIMES)

- Asian countries unexpectedly clashed with the United States and the European Union over a Malaysian proposal to review the Universal Declaration on Human Rights and other key United Nations documents. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Development Budget Coordinating Council will start to review the government's seven to eight percent Gross National Product (GNP) growth target at a meeting on Thursday, a senior official of the National Economic and Development Authority said. (BUSINESSWORLD/TODAY/PHILIPPINE STAR/INQUIRER)
- The Central Bank is looking into the possibility of regulating the parallel foreign exchange markets to prevent a shift of liquidity to these markets. (BUSINESS DAILY/MANILA CHRONICLE/MALAYA)
- The Department of Finance expects second quarter GNP to be higher than the 6.1 percent registered in the first three months of the year. (TIMES JOURNAL)

- A business group, the Federation of Philippine Industries, said it will oppose any increase in fuel prices in the next two months as it is unjustifiable despite the depreciation of the peso. (BULLETIN)
